title: Founder vs investor equity disputes in startups
p1:
A startup can raise millions and still fall apart over a few percentage points.

The biggest equity battles often begin long before investors enter the picture.
p2:
Many founders believe equity disputes happen because investors want too much ownership. The surprising reality: many conflicts come from unclear expectations about control, dilution, and future decisions.

A founder may own 60% today, but future funding rounds can reduce that share. Investors may also have rights that affect major decisions, even without owning the majority.
p3:
Equity is not just about the percentage written on paper. It represents ownership, influence, and alignment between people building the company.

A simple cap table discussion early on can prevent years of conflict. Founders and investors should clearly define ownership, decision-making rights, and what happens when new money enters the business.

The best partnerships are built on transparency before disagreements begin.
conclusion: What do you think causes more startup equity disputes: unclear agreements at the beginning or changing expectations after growth?
